chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadl, from Abdullah ibn Bakir, from al-Bukayr, from al-Ala' ibn Ayn, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
In the book of Ali (peace be upon him), the blood money for a hunting dog is forty dirhams.

key_terms.دِرْهَمًا: Dirham, a historical silver coin used as currency
key_terms.دِيَة: Blood money or financial compensation for damage or death

ai.seo_question: What is the blood money (diyah) for a hunting dog according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* cites a ruling attributed to Imam Ali (peace be upon him) via the chain of al-Barqi, establishing the blood-money (diyah) for a hunting dog at forty dirhams. This specific valuation highlights the early juristic recognition of working animals as property with defined economic worth, reflecting the practical legal frameworks developed during the Imamate period. It underscores the continuity of Ali’s legal authority in matters of civil compensation within Shia scholarly tradition.
